lesson_title: Family Trees and Fair Counts: Geometry and Probability
hook_text: 37 players in a class of 36? Your Venn diagram just confessed.
clip_script: In a class of thirty-six, twenty-two play hockey, fifteen play tennis, nine play both. How many play hockey or tennis? Not twenty-two plus fifteen — that counts the nine double-sport players twice. Correct count: twenty-two plus fifteen minus nine — twenty-eight. And so eight play neither. The Venn diagram shows it at a glance: fill the overlap FIRST with nine, then hockey-only is thirteen, tennis-only is six, and the outside region holds the remaining eight.
visual_style: Two overlapping circles filling with player icons, nine of them flashing double in red before the subtraction sweeps the duplicates away, the totals clicking into 28 and 8.
mood: Detective audit with a satisfying balance-the-books ending.
pacing: Quick setup, freeze on the double-counted nine, clean resolution as the regions total 36.
call_to_action: Watch the full revision sweep — shapes, coordinates, chance and data in one session.
